The PSNR in dB against the original, for images of 160 by 160 pixels saved with Pillow's JPEG encoder at each quality, without chroma subsampling, and decoded again. The filter is told the true quality of the file. The last two columns use 4 and 64 shifted grids. On the colored squares, whose sharp color edges repeat every 20 pixels, 4 grids beat 64, and 64 grids even fall below the JPEG at low quality. Averaging many grids also blurs sharp edges, most of all in Cb and Cr, whose table is coarse. The colored squares are the scene of the dehazing example. The Siemens star has many strong edges, where ringing is worst.
